Dear Requester,
­
Thank you for your correspondence regarding your request for information under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) 2000.

Background to your request

We received your original correspondence on 27 June 2026. Since the information requested related to mapping information which is dealt with as part of our routine business, we forwarded your request to our Customer Service Centre (CSC) on 30 June 2026 and confirmed this via our email, also dated 30 June 2026. Regrettably, our CSC team missed the request, and you didn’t receive a response as promised, for which we apologise, once again.

We received your subsequent request for information as a result of the above, on 20 October 2026. I have set out an extract of the correspondence as follows:

Extract of email dated 20 October 2026

“1. Two parts of my email of 27 June asked for recorded information, not for advice. They asked whether Ordnance Survey holds (a) "any map revision notes, resurvey information, or internal documentation explaining changes in naming or label placement for this area between approximately 1950 and 1975", and (b) "any guidance or archival material explaining how estate names or farm names were assigned, repositioned, or reinterpreted across map editions in this period". Please deal with those two parts as a request for information under section 1 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, or under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 if you consider the information environmental.

2. For each of (a) and (b), please confirm or deny whether the information is held (section 1(1)(a)). The site is at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, within the area of County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, with the map references I gave (38-1-608 and 38-1-334).

3. To make (a) as precise as possible, it covers, for the large-scale (1:2,500 and 1:10,560) plans of this site published between 1950 and 1975: the revision or resurvey dates; any name sheet, name book or field revision record for the names "Ty Mawr", "Great House" or "Great House Farm"; and any record of who supplied or authorised a name or a change to it (for example, an owner, an occupier, a local authority or HM Land Registry), in what capacity, and when.

4. If any of this has been transferred to The National Archives, please give the reference instead of treating that part as not held. I have found that object name books for County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW (1898–1942) are at The National Archives as OS 35/2503. Please tell me whether Ordnance Survey holds anything later of the same kind for this area. If records of this kind were destroyed, please give the disposal schedule or policy that applied and, if recorded, the date.”


We emailed you on 26 October to advise we were having trouble identifying the exact location which was the subject of your request. I have set out the extract of our email and your response to our request for clarification, which was received on 26 October.

Extract of OS clarification request email dated 26 October 2026

“Using the information provided, the only Great House Farm near Llandough we can find is: GREAT HOUSE FARM, LLANDOUGH, COWBRIDGE, [postcode redacted]. However, we cannot find any reference to this address being referred to as Ty Mawr.

We have another location in the vicinity, where we have found a property called Ty Mawr, but no reference to Great House or Great House Farm. I have attached a screenshot of a map we have pulled from the National Library of Scotland which shows this area in approximately 1950, circled in red.

Please can you confirm which address / area is correct.  This will enable us to provide an appropriate and accurate response to your request.”

Extract of your response to our request for clarification dated 26 October 2026

Thank you for your email of 26 October 2026. I confirm that the site is Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, beside St Dochdwy’s Church at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, near Penarth and Cardiff. Its location identifiers are Heneb/GGAT HER GGAT02038s, RCAHMW NPRN 20182 and grid reference ST16707335. The later development address recorded for the site is Church View Close, [postcode redacted]. The relevant mapping area is County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, including map references 38-1-608 and 38-1-334.

Those location and map identifiers should be used as the primary means of identifying the site. The following farm, estate and locality wordings are supporting search terms drawn from different records and periods. They are not all interchangeable names, and their appearance in a source does not by itself establish that they refer to the same building, parcel, estate boundary or title.

Farm and farmhouse nomenclature

Please consider these forms when searching: “Great House Farm”; “Great House Farm, Llandough”; “Great House Farm (GGAT02038s)”; “Great House”; “Great house”; “Greathouse”; “Tŷ Mawr”; “Ty Mawr”; “Ty-mawr”; “Ty Mawr Farm”; “Ty Mawr (Great House)”; “Ty Mawr, Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Cydfin Farm”; “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”; “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”; “Cedfin”; “Cydwin”; “Cedwyn”; “Cedfyn”; “Cefin”; “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm”; “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm”; “Llandough Church Farm”; “Church Farm”; “former Great House Farm”; “a 3.4 acre site located adjacent St. Dochdwy Parish Church”; and “LLANDOUGH FARM (Ideal Homes Wales)”. The map form “Ty-mawr” is also recorded on an Ordnance Survey 25-inch map, although the edition and its precise relationship to the site have not been confirmed.

The source status matters. The National Library of Wales Bute catalogue lists “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)” within a 1552 - 1824 catalogue range; that range is not a specific date for the Ty Mawr wording. The 1824 Stewart survey, plan 19, records “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” (Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1). Historical directories use “Great house” and “Greathouse”. The checked 1881 census image reads “Llandough Home Farm”; “Land Doc Home Farm” is a reported competing transcription, and “R-W-S-S Farm / Reese’s Farm” does not appear on that checked page. “Cydwin” and “Cedwyn” are reported research leads whose underlying 16th-century documents have not been verified; “Cedfyn” and “Cefin” are retained as search forms without a confirmed primary occurrence. “Llandough Church Farm” and “Church Farm” are source-specific terms whose connection to this site is not established by the cited records. The 1994 Ideal Homes Wales plan uses “LLANDOUGH FARM” for this development site, while other records use Llandough Farm for a separate farmstead; please distinguish records by their mapped location rather than by that wording alone.

Other indexed phrases, including “an 800-year-old house”, “the ten-roomed house”, “ancient Welsh house” and “the farm / the whole of the farm”, are descriptions rather than established property names.

Estate and associated-place nomenclature

For relevant records concerning the wider surrounding area, please also consider “Cedwyn Estate”, “Cydwin”, “Cydfin Farm or Ty Mawr Farm, (107 a.)”, “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm” and “Cwm Cydfin Wood”. “Cedwyn Estate” is the family’s working name for the wider historic estate, not a period name established by the records cited here. “Cydwin” is reported from a 1547 family research note whose underlying document is not held; the Bute catalogue wording and the 1824 survey wording have the source limits described above. “Cwm Cydfin Wood” appears in a 1902 Bute sale catalogue. These names are search aids for relevant site and surrounding-area records, not a claim that each denotes the same holding or proves the estate’s extent or title.

Town and locality nomenclature

Please also consider “Llandough-juxta-Penarth”; “Llandough near Penarth”; “Llandough near Cardiff”; “Llandough, Penarth”; “Llandough, Cardiff”; “Llandough”; “Landoche-juxta-Cardif”; “Llandough / Leckwith”; “Penarth Road, Llandough”; “Urban District of Penarth”; “Llandochau”; and “CF64” / “Church View Close, [postcode redacted]”. “Landoche-juxta-Cardif” is a historical locator for the manor, not proof that every holding in a record bearing that locator is this farm. “Llandough / Leckwith” is neighbouring parish and manorial context, not another name for the farm. “Urban District of Penarth” is a historical local-government description. The location-name references are kept separate from the farm and estate name references.

The three nomenclature pages and the fuller location-name and name-variation notes are here:

Farm: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/great-house-farm/
Estate: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/cedwyn-estate/
Locality: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/nomenclature/c/llandough/
Location-name notes: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wiki/great-house-farm/location-name-nomenclature/
Name-variation notes: https://cedwyn.bucklerfamily.estate/wiki/great-house-farm/name-variations/

My substantive request remains the recorded-information request set out in my email of 20 October 2026. In particular, for the large-scale 1:2,500 and 1:10,560 plans of this site published between 1950 and 1975, I seek any revision or resurvey dates; map revision notes, name sheets, name books or field revision records concerning “Ty Mawr”, “Great House” or “Great House Farm”; and any record of who supplied or authorised a name or change, in what capacity and when. I also seek any relevant guidance or archival material on how farm or estate names were assigned, repositioned or reinterpreted across map editions in that period. Please confirm or deny whether each category is held under section 1(1)(a) of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, or under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 if applicable.

If any relevant material has been transferred to The National Archives, please provide its reference. I have identified OS 35/2503 for object name books for Glamorgan 47 NW covering 1898 - 1942; please also say whether Ordnance Survey holds later records of the same kind for this area. If relevant records were destroyed, please provide the applicable disposal schedule or policy and the date of disposal if recorded. If any part cannot be answered as framed, please provide advice and assistance under section 16.”

We also received your later email of 26 October, which provided additional information to help us identify the site.  As we were able to confirm the site from the above, and your email did not contain a further request for recorded information, we have not set this out in this response.

Our response

We have dealt with your request under the Freedom of Information Act (2000).  Having clarified the original request to ascertain the exact location, we take each of your requests in turn, as follows:


  1.  Two parts of my email of 27 June asked for recorded information, not for advice. They asked whether Ordnance Survey holds (a) “any map revision notes, resurvey information, or internal documentation explaining changes in naming or label placement for this area between approximately 1950 and 1975”, and (b) “any guidance or archival material explaining how estate names or farm names were assigned, repositioned, or reinterpreted across map editions in this period”. Please deal with those two parts as a request for information under section 1 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000, or under the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 if you consider the information environmental.


This information is not held.


  1.  For each of (a) and (b), please confirm or deny whether the information is held (section 1(1)(a)). The site is at Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Vale of Glamorgan, within the area of County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW, with the map references I gave (38-1-608 and 38-1-334).



This relates to request 1 above and we confirm that the information is not held.



  1.  To make (a) as precise as possible, it covers, for the large-scale (1:2,500 and 1:10,560) plans of this site published between 1950 and 1975: the revision or resurvey dates; any name sheet, name book or field revision record for the names "Ty Mawr", "Great House" or "Great House Farm"; and any record of who supplied or authorised a name or a change to it (for example, an owner, an occupier, a local authority or HM Land Registry), in what capacity, and when.



This information is not held


  1.  If any of this has been transferred to The National Archives, please give the reference instead of treating that part as not held. I have found that object name books for County Series sheet Glamorgan 47 NW (1898–1942) are at The National Archives as OS 35/2503. Please tell me whether Ordnance Survey holds anything later of the same kind for this area. If records of this kind were destroyed, please give the disposal schedule or policy that applied and, if recorded, the date.

This information is not held. Please see below advice and assistance.

Advice and Assistance

Under the duty to provide information and assistance in accordance with section 16 of the FOIA, we can provide the following information which may assist you in this matter:

Your clarification response confirmed to us that the map we sent you with our email of 26 October 2026, is the correct region for the property, which is the subject of your request. We have found some archive maps. They show the area from: 1947 (published in 1950); 1965; 1971; 1977 and 1989.

This mapping shows we had the property named as Ty-Mawr in 1947 and it changed to Ty Mawr Farm between 1965 and 1971. It was still called that in 1989. There is no mention of any other name at the location. The name would only have been changed if there was clear evidence either from a sign on the property or confirmation from the owner / occupier.

Unfortunately, the relevant Object Name Book for the area, which would have shown any name changes and who authorised them is not held by OS and The National Archive record states ‘Missing at Transfer’  ST1673. Missing at transfer | The National Archives<https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/details/r/C11414033>

We do not hold any archive records detailing the reasons that prompted any changes to our mapping.  OS maintain the National Map, which is over 600 million features of Britain’s landscape.  Once a change is made, the map itself serves as the record of any change.

Thank you for your emails to the Bute Collection at Mount Stuart.  As you are aware we are unable to respond to enquiries at this time and this will be reviewed in January 2027 due to staffing levels.  The research spaces are fully booked between now and Christmas.

Subject: Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth

Dear Requester,

Thank you for your emails dated 29 October 2026 regarding Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth.

We have considered the information contained within your email and the additional search terms you have provided.

The Environmental Information Regulations 2004 (EIR) provide a right of access to recorded environmental information held by a public authority. Regulation 2(1) defines environmental information and includes information concerning matters such as the state of the environment, factors affecting the environment, and measures or activities affecting or likely to affect the environment.

Having considered your correspondence, we do not consider that the information you have requested regarding the disconnection, shut off, cap, termination or otherwise interference with the water supply to Great House Farm constitutes a request for environmental information falling within the definition at Regulation 2(1) of the EIR.

The information requested relates to the disconnection of a specific property. The fact that information concerns a water supply to a property does not, of itself, make it “environmental information” for the purposes of regulation 2(1) of the Environmental Information Regulations 2004. The information must fall within one or more of the categories in regulation 2(1). The requested information concerns the fact and circumstances of the property's disconnection. It does not describe the state of any element of the environment, such as water, air, soil or land, within regulation 2(1)(a), nor does it concern a factor such as a substance, energy, noise, radiation, waste, emission, discharge or other release which affects or is likely to affect those elements within regulation 2(1)(b). Further, the disconnection is not a measure or activity affecting or likely to affect environmental elements or factors, or as one designed to protect them, within regulation 2(1)(c). The remaining limbs of regulation 2(1), concerning reports on environmental legislation, relevant economic analyses, and human health and safety or built structures insofar as they are affected by environmental elements, factors, measures or activities, are likewise not engaged.

As the request is directed to the disconnection of this property rather than to any environmental state, effect, factor, measure or activity within regulation 2(1), the information does not fall within the definition of environmental information under the EIR.

Even if this information were considered to be environmental information for the purposes of the Regulations, DCWW would have to refuse the request under Regulation 12(4)(a) as we do not hold the information requested. We do not hold the historical information sought. In accordance with our Retention Policy, any customer or property records from the 1980s that may have existed from that period would fall outside of our data retention periods., and we would no longer hold records dating back to that time. We are also unaware of any other public authority that may hold this information.

For this reason, we are unable to carry out the additional historical searches requested or provide an audit trail identifying search terms and systems in respect of information that is no longer held.

Your email also requested confirmation as to whether any surviving historic records, indexes, work-order records or archived material relating to Great House Farm/Ty Mawr exist. Some such information could constitute environmental information, depending on the nature of the information held and whether it fell within the definition of environmental information in Regulation 2(1). However, for the reasons set out above, we do not hold any historic records, indexes, work-order records or archived material falling within the scope of your request. We are therefore unable to determine whether any such information, if it existed, would constitute environmental information. In any event, as we do not hold the requested information, the request would fall to be refused under Regulation 12(4)(a). We are also unaware of any other public authority that may hold this information.

We hope this clarifies our position.

Thank you
